item.title: In Texas, Talarico Inspires a Recurring Blue-Tinted Dream
item.description: After a dry spell of more than three decades, Democrats are daring (yet again) to believe they can win one or more top-of-the-ballot races in a vast and stubbornly red state.
item.dc:creator: Robert Draper
item.media:credit: Desiree Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: According to recent polls, James Talarico, a Democratic state legislator, is ahead of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general, in the race for a U.S. Senate seat.

item.title: Democrats May Have Found the Recipe for Flipping Red-State Senate Seats
item.description: Five new Times/Siena polls continue a run of strong results for the party in states that President Trump won easily in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Nate Cohn
item.media:credit: Illustration by Tyler Comrie; Spatula photograph by Issarawat Tattong/Getty Images

item.title: Trump, Putin, Ukraine and an Oil Deal: 5 Takeaways
item.description: A proposal to bolster relations with the Kremlin through the purchase of Russian energy assets is striking even for an administration that regularly mixes personal business interests with foreign policy.
item.dc:creator: Eric Lipton and Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: Cars waited to refuel at a Lukoil fuel station amid fuel shortages in August.

item.title: How Trump’s Deportation Policies Have Rocked a South Florida House Race
item.description: Representative María Elvira Salazar, a Republican, ran an ad criticizing the Trump administration. It may have jolted other Republicans — and drawn attention to her Democratic opponent.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:description: Representative María Elvira Salazar ran an ad criticizing the Trump administration’s deportation policies, angering the president and possibly emboldening other Republicans around the country.

item.title: U.S.-Russia Talks on Ukraine Now Involve an Oil Deal Tied to Trump Allies
item.description: President Vladimir V. Putin brought up a sale of Russian energy assets with President Trump’s envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, pushing a deal that raises new questions about conflicts of interest.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski and Eric Lipton
item.category: Office of Foreign Assets Control (United States Treasury)
item.media:credit: Gianni Cipriano for The New York Times
item.media:description: The negotiations about the Lukoil deal show that personal business interests in President Trump’s inner circle are also in play. Lukoil is Russia’s biggest private oil company.

item.title: F.D.A. Found Cyclospora During Taylor Farms Inspection in Mexico
item.description: The discovery adds strong evidence that the outbreak that sickened thousands over the summer originated in a grower’s field or processing facility.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett, Alice Callahan and Caroline Hopkins Legaspi
item.media:credit: Fred Ramos for The New York Times
item.media:description: Over the course of the summer, the cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms caused nearly 13,000 illnesses, 570 hospitalizations and two deaths in 21 states.

item.title: National Science Foundation Diverted $1.4 Billion in Science Funds Mandated by Congress
item.description: The move, affecting about one-fifth of the National Science Foundation’s primary research budget, is the latest sign of how the White House is asserting more control over grants.
item.dc:creator: Adam Sella, Christopher Flavelle and Irena Hwang
item.media:description: Some National Science Foundation divisions pulled back research proposals in order to comply with White House guidance to carry over funds.

item.title: Unusual Issues in Court at Guantánamo Stand Out as a Case Finally Heads to Trial
item.description: Prosecutors want remote testimony for witnesses unable or unwilling to travel to Guantánamo. The defense wants jurors to be told that, guilty or innocent, the defendant will not go free.
item.dc:creator: Carol Rosenberg
item.media:credit: Marisa Schwartz Taylor/The New York Times
item.media:description: A sign at the legal complex at Guantánamo Bay, seen in 2023.

item.title: Trump to Name Jay Clayton to Serve as A.I. Czar
item.description: The director of national intelligence will help develop new policies, and potentially regulations, for the rapidly evolving technology.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes and Tyler Pager
item.category: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
item.media:description: Jay Clayton’s added role comes as the Trump administration faces pressure to develop new regulations or safety standards for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Flurry of Lawsuits Shows Both Parties Preparing for Post-Election Challenges
item.description: Republicans are using the courts to hunt for noncitizen voters. Democrats worry the G.O.P. is trying make it harder for eligible voters to cast ballots — and paving the way to try to toss valid election results.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: A voter casting a ballot at Miller Elementary School in Dearborn, Mich., during the state’s primary in August. Scores of lawsuits from the two major political parties and their allies reveal the likely battle lines for post-election challenges.

item.title: Sales of Hulking Pickups and S.U.V.s Sag as Fuel Prices Soar
item.description: Sales of big pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles have dipped as more Americans buy hybrids and smaller cars.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.category: Sports Utility Vehicles and Light Trucks
item.media:description: Sales of the Chevrolet Silverado were up, but the growth came from a light-duty version of the truck. Sales of heavy-duty Silverados slumped as Americans shift away from full-size pickups and S.U.V.s.

item.title: The Rich People Democrats Aren’t Talking About
